A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PrefixKV work, with matching authors, algorithm, and retained experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v3 ends with references; v4 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLaVA and Qwen-VL evaluations, inference measurements, ablations, and generated examples in Section 4.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and reports additional robustness, language-model, and visual-question-answering experiments, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The attention-based ranking, binary-search allocation, offline estimation, and decoding eviction procedure remain unchanged. v4 additionally evaluates combining PrefixKV with 4-bit KIVI quantization in Section 4.3, introducing a limited hybrid compression variant.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained LLaVA-Description and MM-Vet evaluations, v4 adds LongBench and Needle-in-a-HayStack language tasks, constructed multi-round and long-text VQA scenarios, and high-resolution MM-Vet evaluation using LLaVA-NeXT. Table 14 and Appendix B therefore substantially broaden task requirements and input conditions.

E2.justification: PyramidKV, already evaluated in v3's prefix-configuration analysis, joins the main 7B comparisons in Tables 1–2. v4 also evaluates KIVI against PrefixKV in Table 15, expanding the comparison to a distinct quantization approach. Local, H2O, and Elastic remain in their corresponding visual-model comparisons.

E3.justification: Existing principal experiments retain their reported settings. Added protocols include a 128-token cache budget for LLaMA-3-8B long-context evaluations, compression-budget comparisons with KIVI, and 50% budgets for the additional VQA scenarios. Tables 8–11 also introduce controlled calibration-domain, instruction-length, search-tolerance, and search-step experiments.

E4.justification: v4 retains the existing offline/online, sample-count, merging, and feature-disturbance analyses. It adds allocation-deviation statistics, calibration-domain and instruction-length robustness, and binary-search sensitivity analyses in Tables 7–11. Appendix B adds the Qwen-VL allocation profile, while Appendix C replaces v3's single chat example with five different case studies.

E5.justification: Table 7 newly reports standard deviations of online allocation ratios across samples and mean absolute differences from offline allocation. This adds statistical summaries beyond v3's sample visualizations. These characterize allocation variability; neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-seed results.

E6.justification: Shared LLaVA, Qwen-VL, timing, and existing ablation scores remain unchanged after matching relocated tables. v4 adds PyramidKV ROUGE and LLaVA-Description results, robustness measurements, new benchmark scores, and replacement qualitative examples. For example, Table 14 reports PrefixKV scores of 37.5 on LongBench and 97.6 on Needle, versus PyramidKV's 37.1 and 97.3, under newly reported settings.

T1.justification: The importance definitions, cumulative-priority construction, budget constraint, binary-search reasoning, and merging mathematics are retained. Several equations become inline or are renumbered. Appendix A supplies standard formulas for the already-used PPL and ROUGE-L metrics, without introducing new theory or changing their definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about adaptive global prefix allocation, contextual-information preservation, competitive generation quality, and inference efficiency, including the 1.8× speedup example. The added abstract definition of 'prefix' restates the explanation already present in v3.

C2.justification: v4 adds a budget-dependent interpretation of pruning versus quantization and explicitly hypothesizes a hierarchical explanation for the W-shaped allocation pattern in Appendix B. Appendix D newly acknowledges untested larger models and unexplored acceleration combinations. These extend the explanations and applicability boundaries while retaining the central information-preservation interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies PyTorch, NVIDIA 3090 GPUs, and temperature 0.2 for the uncompressed ROUGE reference comparison; v3 only described that temperature as nonzero. These are additional disclosures, without evidence that the existing experiments changed. The A100 timing setup and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused: broad discussions of 3D perception, semantic understanding, and efficient vision architectures are reduced, while KV-cache literature and positioning against prior layer-wise allocation methods expand. Added works include KVMerger, ZipVL, Look-M, InfiniGen, FastV, and KIVI. PyramidKV itself was already cited and compared in v3.

P1.justification: Most methodological prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v4 selectively shortens related work and explanations, clarifies terminology, reverses the order of the efficiency and prefix-configuration analyses, and adds acknowledgments and organized appendices. The retained narrative undergoes limited editing rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The two-column v3 is reformatted into a single-column NeurIPS layout with wrapped figures and algorithm text, rearranged tables, and several compact displays placed side by side. Main tables gain PyramidKV rows, additional analysis tables and Figure 6 appear, and five appendix chat displays replace the earlier example. Figures 1–5 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens validation of offline allocation: Tables 7–11 test domain, instruction-length, and search sensitivity beyond v3's existing sample-count and offline/online checks. Main-table PyramidKV comparisons, the explicit KIVI tradeoff, and challenging long-context and visual scenarios address important gaps in competitive and applicability evidence. Implementation disclosures and stated limitations improve transparency. Some added benchmark protocols remain briefly documented, but the gains in empirical support and balanced comparison are substantial.
